text: Hadley v. Baxendale, 9 Exch. 341 (1854). Consequential damages for breach of contract are recoverable only if they were reasonably foreseeable at the time of contract formation. Foundational case for contract damages analysis.

Celotex Corp. v. Catrett, 477 U.S. 317 (1986). Moving party on summary judgment need not negate opponent's claim but must show absence of genuine issue of material fact. Defines burden of production on summary judgment.

Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662 (2009). To survive a motion to dismiss, a complaint must contain sufficient factual matter to state a claim that is plausible on its face. Establishes plausibility pleading standard.

McDonnell Douglas Corp. v. Green, 411 U.S. 792 (1973). Establishes burden-shifting framework for employment discrimination claims under Title VII. Plaintiff must show prima facie case, then burden shifts to employer for legitimate reason.

Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, 509 U.S. 579 (1993). Trial judge serves as gatekeeper for expert testimony admissibility. Expert testimony must be based on sufficient facts, reliable principles, and reliably applied methodology.

International Shoe Co. v. Washington, 326 U.S. 310 (1945). Due process requires that a defendant have certain minimum contacts with the forum state such that maintenance of the suit does not offend traditional notions of fair play and substantial justice.

Erie Railroad Co. v. Tompkins, 304 U.S. 64 (1938). Federal courts sitting in diversity must apply state substantive law and federal procedural law. Overruled Swift v. Tyson. Foundational choice-of-law doctrine.

Palsgraf v. Long Island Railroad Co., 248 N.Y. 339 (1928). Negligence liability requires a duty owed to the particular plaintiff. Defendant owes no duty to unforeseeable plaintiffs. Cardozo majority establishes foreseeability test for duty.
Marbury v. Madison, 5 U.S. 137 (1803). Supreme Court has authority of judicial review to declare acts of Congress unconstitutional. Establishes judicial supremacy in constitutional interpretation.
Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436 (1966). Prior to custodial interrogation, police must inform suspects of their Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination and Sixth Amendment right to counsel.

Texaco Inc. v. Pennzoil Co., 729 S.W.2d 768 (Tex. App. 1987). Tortious interference with contractual relations established where third party intentionally disrupted binding agreement. $10.53 billion judgment.

Riegel v. Medtronic Inc., 552 U.S. 312 (2008). Medical Device Amendments preempt state-law claims that are different from or in addition to federal requirements for Class III medical devices with PMA approval.

Anderson v. Liberty Lobby Inc., 477 U.S. 242 (1986). On summary judgment, court must view evidence in light most favorable to non-moving party. Genuine issue exists where reasonable jury could find for non-movant.

BMW of North America v. Gore, 517 U.S. 559 (1996). Due process limits punitive damages. Three guideposts: (1) degree of reprehensibility, (2) ratio to actual harm, (3) comparison to civil penalties. Ratios exceeding 10:1 suspect.

Twombly (Bell Atlantic Corp. v. Twombly), 550 U.S. 544 (2007). Complaint must allege enough facts to state a claim to relief that is plausible on its face. Retirement of Conley v. Gibson no-set-of-facts standard.

Strickland v. Washington, 466 U.S. 668 (1984). Ineffective assistance of counsel requires showing: (1) counsel's performance was deficient, and (2) deficiency prejudiced the defense. Strong presumption of reasonable professional assistance.

Jacob & Youngs v. Kent, 230 N.Y. 239 (1921). Substantial performance doctrine: where breach is minor and unintentional, damages measured by difference in value rather than cost of replacement. Cardozo opinion.

Upjohn Co. v. United States, 449 U.S. 383 (1981). Attorney-client privilege in corporate context extends beyond control group to communications with lower-level employees when made for purpose of obtaining legal advice.

Hickman v. Taylor, 329 U.S. 495 (1947). Work product doctrine protects materials prepared by attorney in anticipation of litigation from discovery. Qualified privilege for factual work product, near-absolute for mental impressions.

Markman v. Westview Instruments, 517 U.S. 370 (1996). Patent claim construction is a matter of law for the court, not fact for the jury. Judge determines meaning and scope of patent claims at Markman hearing.

Kelo v. City of New London, 545 U.S. 469 (2005). Public use requirement of Fifth Amendment Takings Clause satisfied by economic development purpose. Government may transfer private property to another private entity for development.

Lucas v. South Carolina Coastal Council, 505 U.S. 1003 (1992). Regulation that deprives owner of all economically beneficial use constitutes a per se taking requiring compensation under the Fifth Amendment.

Burlington Industries v. Ellerth, 524 U.S. 742 (1998). Employer vicariously liable for supervisor harassment resulting in tangible employment action. Affirmative defense available when no tangible action taken.

Alice Corp. v. CLS Bank International, 573 U.S. 208 (2014). Abstract ideas implemented on generic computer are not patent-eligible under 35 U.S.C. 101. Two-step test: (1) is claim directed to abstract idea, (2) is there inventive concept.

Loving v. Virginia, 388 U.S. 1 (1967). Anti-miscegenation statutes violate Equal Protection and Due Process clauses of Fourteenth Amendment. Marriage is a fundamental right that cannot be restricted by race.

Meinhard v. Salmon, 249 N.Y. 458 (1928). Fiduciary duty between joint venturers requires punctilio of an honor the most sensitive. Co-venturer must disclose business opportunity to partner. Cardozo opinion on fiduciary loyalty.

Terry v. Ohio, 392 U.S. 1 (1968). Police officer may conduct brief investigatory stop based on reasonable suspicion of criminal activity. Pat-down search permitted if officer reasonably believes suspect is armed.

Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer, 343 U.S. 579 (1952). President lacks inherent authority to seize private property absent congressional authorization. Jackson concurrence establishes three-zone framework for executive power.

Adarand Constructors v. Pena, 515 U.S. 200 (1995). All racial classifications by federal government subject to strict scrutiny review. Must be narrowly tailored to serve a compelling governmental interest.

Wal-Mart Stores v. Dukes, 564 U.S. 338 (2011). Class certification under Rule 23(a) requires showing that common questions predominate. Commonality requires common contention capable of classwide resolution.

New York Times Co. v. Sullivan, 376 U.S. 254 (1964). Public officials must prove actual malice (knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard for truth) to recover in defamation action. First Amendment protection for public discourse.

Chevron U.S.A. v. Natural Resources Defense Council, 467 U.S. 837 (1984). Courts defer to reasonable agency interpretation of ambiguous statute the agency administers. Two-step framework for judicial review of agency action.

Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo, 603 U.S. ___ (2024). Overruled Chevron deference. Courts must exercise independent judgment in deciding whether an agency has acted within its statutory authority. APA Section 706 governs.

Bostock v. Clayton County, 590 U.S. 644 (2020). Title VII prohibition on sex discrimination encompasses discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. Textualist interpretation of 'because of sex.'

Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission, 558 U.S. 310 (2010). First Amendment prohibits government from restricting independent political expenditures by corporations, associations, and labor unions.

Carpenter v. United States, 585 U.S. 296 (2018). Accessing historical cell-site location information constitutes a search under Fourth Amendment requiring a warrant. Digital privacy expectations in modern era.
Waffle House (EEOC v. Waffle House), 534 U.S. 279 (2002). EEOC retains authority to pursue victim-specific judicial relief regardless of mandatory arbitration agreement between employer and employee.

AT&T Mobility v. Concepcion, 563 U.S. 333 (2011). Federal Arbitration Act preempts state law rules that prohibit class-wide arbitration waivers in consumer contracts. Arbitration agreements enforceable per their terms.
eBay Inc. v. MercExchange, 547 U.S. 388 (2006). Patent holders must satisfy traditional four-factor test for permanent injunction. No presumption of irreparable harm from patent infringement alone.
Spokeo v. Robins, 578 U.S. 330 (2016). Article III standing requires concrete injury, not merely statutory violation. Bare procedural violation without concrete harm insufficient for standing.

Bristol-Myers Squibb v. Superior Court, 582 U.S. 255 (2017). Specific personal jurisdiction requires that claims arise out of or relate to defendant's contacts with forum state. Rejects sliding-scale approach.

TransUnion LLC v. Ramirez, 594 U.S. 413 (2021). Plaintiffs must demonstrate concrete harm to have Article III standing. Mere risk of future harm from inaccurate credit report insufficient where report not disseminated.

Jones v. Hendrix, 599 U.S. 465 (2023). Federal prisoners cannot use 28 U.S.C. 2241 habeas petitions to challenge convictions based on intervening changes in statutory interpretation that were unavailable on direct appeal.

Sackett v. EPA, 598 U.S. 651 (2023). Clean Water Act jurisdiction over wetlands requires continuous surface connection to waters of the United States. Narrows EPA regulatory authority over isolated wetlands.

Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard, 600 U.S. 181 (2023). Race-conscious admissions programs at Harvard and UNC violate Equal Protection Clause. Overrules Grutter v. Bollinger compelling interest in educational diversity.

Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, 597 U.S. 215 (2022). Constitution does not confer right to abortion. Overrules Roe v. Wade and Planned Parenthood v. Casey. Returns regulation of abortion to the states.

Viking River Cruises v. Moriana, 596 U.S. 639 (2022). FAA preempts California rule prohibiting division of PAGA claims into individual and non-individual components. Arbitration agreements can compel individual PAGA claims.

Counterman v. Colorado, 600 U.S. 66 (2023). True threats prosecution under First Amendment requires proof that defendant had subjective understanding of threatening nature of statements. Recklessness standard sufficient.

Groff v. DeJoy, 600 U.S. 447 (2023). Title VII religious accommodation imposes undue hardship only when accommodation would result in substantial increased costs in relation to conduct of employer's business. Clarifies de minimis standard.

Twitter v. Taamneh, 598 U.S. 471 (2023). Social media platforms not liable for aiding and abetting terrorism under Anti-Terrorism Act merely by providing generally available platforms. Requires knowing and substantial assistance.
